issues.description: Method getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor in class Lecture has conflicting return types: the problem statement's UML (class diagram) declares getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): double, while the solution implementation declares public int getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(). This mismatch changes the semantics (integer division vs. floating-point division) and can confuse students or cause tests/example code that expect a double to fail or produce truncated values.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation match the UML/specification by changing the method signature in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to return double and perform floating-point division, e.g.: public double getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() { return (double) getTotalNumberOfStudents() / getNumberOfTutors(); } Optionally guard against division by zero (e.g., return 0.0 when numberOfTutors is 0). Alternatively, if an integer result was intended, update the problem statement/UML to specify an int return type and clarify that integer division/truncation is expected.
